prompt: Complete validateForm so a sign-up panel writes a specific message into each field's own error label, sets a summary like "2 problems", and returns true only when everything passes.
explanation: Per-field error labels mean each field gets its own if/else-if chain, ordered from the most basic failure (empty) to the most specific, so the user sees the message that matters most. Parsing the age has to happen inside a try/catch because Integer.parseInt throws NumberFormatException on anything that is not a whole number -- that exception is the test, not an accident. Counting the non-empty error labels at the end gives both the summary text and the boolean result from one place, so they can never disagree.
hints: Handle each field with its own if / else if / else chain, and always set the label in every branch -- including the empty string for success.
Wrap Integer.parseInt in try/catch (NumberFormatException) and put the range check inside the try.
Count how many of the three error labels are non-empty; that number decides both the summary wording and the return value.
